statements: Apex Oncology Lab models the number $X$ of successes in $18$ independent trials as binomial, but its success probability is hidden. Calibration gives the exact adjacent-mass ratio $P(X=4)/P(X=3)=\dfrac{45}{28}$. After recovering $p$ from that ratio, the analyst claims $P(X=6)=\dfrac{46829074732984089}{250000000000000000}$. Case note: The result determines whether the quarter-end control file is reopened.

Dover Support Desk independently inspects $20$ cases, each producing the flagged outcome with probability $\dfrac{2}{5}$. If $X$ counts flags, management claims the full multi-term probability of observing at most $6$ flags is $\dfrac{23842875665458}{95367431640625}$, not merely the endpoint mass. Case note: The calculation governs a reserve that cannot be changed after the reporting cutoff.

Granite Blood Bank reports only that a binomial count has mean $9$ and variance $\dfrac{9}{2}$. These two moments must first be used to recover both $p$ and $n$. Based on that recovery, the operations memo claims mean cost $435$ and variance $\dfrac{11025}{2}$. Case note: Management rounded nothing in the source ledger, so the check must remain exact.

Juniper Call Team compares two independent teams. Team A has $25$ attempts with success probability $\dfrac{3}{10}$; Team B has $25$ with probability $\dfrac{17}{25}$. A strong day means at least $13$ successes. After summing both complete upper tails, the director claims B is more than $\dfrac{278}{5}$ times as likely as A to have a strong day. Case note: The source records were independently timestamped and must be reconciled without averaging.

Meridian Vaccine Unit runs system A for $7$ independent attempts at success probability $\dfrac{1}{5}$ and system B for $9$ attempts at $\dfrac{3}{10}$; the two systems are independent. Using zero-success complements before combining the systems, the reliability report claims the probability that exactly one of the two systems records at least one success is $\dfrac{18214318552699}{78125000000000}$. Case note: The result feeds a fixed-price quotation that expires when the review window closes.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

For adjacent binomial masses, the common factors cancel:

$$\dfrac{P(X=4)}{P(X=3)}
=\dfrac{n-3}{4}\dfrac{p}{1-p}$$

Insert the calibrated ratio:

$$\dfrac{15}{4}\dfrac{p}{1-p}
=\dfrac{45}{28}$$

Solving this rational equation gives

$$p=\dfrac{3}{10},\qquad 1-p=\dfrac{7}{10}$$

Now evaluate the requested, different mass:

$$P(X=6)=\binom{18}{6}
\left(\dfrac{3}{10}\right)^{6}
\left(\dfrac{7}{10}\right)^{12}$$

$$=(18564)(\dfrac{729}{1000000})
(\dfrac{13841287201}{1000000000000})$$

$$=\dfrac{46829074732984089}{250000000000000000}\approx 0.1873162989$$

The analyst's exact fraction is $\dfrac{46829074732984089}{250000000000000000}$.

The recomputed result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The fixed trial count, common probability, and independence give

$$X\sim\operatorname{Bin}\left(20,\dfrac{2}{5}\right)$$

The wording includes every integer in the indicated tail:

$$P(X\le 6)=\sum_{x=0}^{6}
\binom{20}{x}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^x
\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{20-x}$$

The included disjoint masses are:

$$P(X=0)=\binom{20}{0}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{0}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{20}\approx 0.0000365616$$

$$P(X=1)=\binom{20}{1}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{19}\approx 0.0004874878$$

$$P(X=2)=\binom{20}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{18}\approx 0.0030874227$$

$$P(X=3)=\binom{20}{3}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{3}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{17}\approx 0.0123496907$$

$$P(X=4)=\binom{20}{4}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{4}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{16}\approx 0.0349907904$$

$$P(X=5)=\binom{20}{5}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{5}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{15}\approx 0.0746470195$$

$$P(X=6)=\binom{20}{6}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{6}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{14}\approx 0.1244116992$$

Adding all $7$ terms gives

$$P(X\le 6)=\dfrac{23842875665457}{95367431640625}
\approx 0.2500106719$$

The management fraction is $\dfrac{23842875665458}{95367431640625}$.

The recomputed result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

For a nondegenerate binomial count,

$$E(X)=np=9$$

$$\operatorname{Var}(X)=np(1-p)=\dfrac{9}{2}$$

Divide variance by mean:

$$1-p=\dfrac{\dfrac{9}{2}}{9}
=\dfrac{1}{2}$$

$$p=\dfrac{1}{2},\qquad
n=\dfrac{9}{\dfrac{1}{2}}=18$$

For $C=120+35X$,

$$E(C)=120+35(9)=435$$

$$\operatorname{Var}(C)=35^2(\dfrac{9}{2})
=\dfrac{11025}{2}$$

The claim gives mean $435$ and variance $\dfrac{11025}{2}$.

The recomputed result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

X_B\sim\operatorname{Bin}(25,\dfrac{17}{25})$$

\binom{25}{x}(\dfrac{3}{10})^x(\dfrac{7}{10})^{25-x}
=\dfrac{21837175657572120603201}{1250000000000000000000000}\approx 0.0174697405$$
